style: Faithful code reconstruction of the supplied Faker Bilibili intro: near-black fine grid, deep glossy crimson extruded T1 mark, five white stars; pink/blue retro-desktop windows bloom behind; a central white flare swallows stars and reveals bouncy white FAKER lettering with thick pink and violet extruded contours. Stop on title; do not include computer-room scene.
font: Lilita One (or local rounded heavy sans matching reference, with per-letter SVG/CSS transforms)
shot_brief: Start already close to the dark red T1 emblem, push in so its top lip becomes a platform, let five glowing white stars settle into one straight row, then lift and rearrange them into a shallow arc. The camera pulls back into a virtual retro desktop with fine graph-paper lines, floating translucent UI panels, violet and cyan edge light and a central red/pink glow. Stars travel toward a bright point and collapse into a flare, which expands into a pastel-white flash; playful white FAKER letters with pink sides and purple extrusion spring into the central foreground on a white pill. Keep full-size FAKER title legible from 4.0 through 5.0 seconds.

catalog_assessment.decision: Custom procedural construction required for the reference-specific T1 geometry, five-star choreography, layered UI tunnel, flare collapse, and multicolor extruded letterforms. Generic logo assembly/caption motion would visibly depart from the requested shot. Borrow only the catalog motion vocabulary; no mandatory generic block substitution.

scenes.motion: Pseudo-3D SVG T1 fills lower 65%; initial scale 1 at center then push 1.45 and translate y+100, so top red lip spans x120..1750 around y640 by .3. Five stars enter separate curved trajectories with white faces and dark crimson side layers, rotate independently then settle straight at x480,720,960,1200,1440 y515. Faint duplicate reflections sit on the logo lip. Near-black fine 90px grid stays visible.

T1 slides below frame. Stars shrink to 90px and form arc at x600,780,960,1140,1320 and y775,710,660,710,775. Grid densifies and becomes 3D tunnel perspective. Translucent bordered retro panels ease from offscreen: top-left small chart, left-edge desktop list, mid-left logo/title card, lower-left trophy silhouettes card, top-right roster, mid-right esports trophy silhouettes card, right-edge cyan wireframe windows. At 1.8 bloom pink top-center and blue edges; by 2.2 desktop is vivid violet-blue-pink, with center vertical magenta region.

White eight-point flare at x960 y440 moves down to y620 and grows. Fine white curving perspective rays connect upper/lower panels to the light. Stars compress in toward center and scale down from .8 to .08 by 3.15. Light wash brightens pink/coral and white; at 3.3 flash fills frame with warm white. Do not use a plain crossfade in place of the expanding radial flare.

Flash recedes into pastel mint/cyan/pink desktop. Independently animated letters white fronts with 8px purple/pink outline and 24px extruded magenta/violet sides spring from .55 to 1.08 then settle. Final word width ~930 at x960 y550, letters uneven baselines and rotations [-8,3,-4,3,4] degrees; F/R slightly taller. White rounded capsule behind baseline, purple/pink underside. Five tiny outlined championship stars arranged below on capsule. Retain grid over background (not title), translucent UI panels, small dots/glints; gentle parallax and restrained shine. Title lockup fully readable by 4.05; hold to 5.0 without transition into room.

implementation_constraints: All visual motion deterministic and seek-safe; paused GSAP master timeline on window.__timelines.
No original video, extracted reference frames or full-frame screenshots as output visuals. Procedural SVG logo, stars, trophy/player silhouettes and HTML desktop panels.
No source watermark recreation; the T1-Faker/bilibili stamp belongs to the source recording, not the intro design.
Maintain near-black/crimson opening for first ~1.5s; do not start with bright purple.
Optional GLSL only for flare/warp background; layered CSS gradients and SVG rays sufficient.
5s final composition intentionally extends FAKER hold ~0.3s beyond source before its computer-room cut.
